query_text: Build a web app for a startup community that gives members a really easy way to jump into the team Discord and Slack from one spot, so nobody has to hunt around for invite links, the home screen shows both community chat buttons clearly with a short description of what each space is for, and there's also a little note about what kind of conversations happen in each one.

Need a web app that is the main tool itself for a small startup, where I can log in and actually do the core work without bouncing between five different services, it should have a clean left-side list of the main tasks or projects I'm working on, a workspace area in the middle where I actually get things done, and everything saves automatically so I never lose progress mid-session.

A tool-style web app for a startup where the main overview screen shows all the key numbers and active tasks in one place, so I can open the browser in the morning and immediately know what needs attention without clicking through five different spots, with a sidebar listing my ongoing projects and a main area that shows status updates and recent activity for each one.

Build a website for a school or educational institution that covers the main things visitors need, like a clear intro to what the school is about, a list of programs offered with short descriptions, contact info, and a map showing where the campus is, all laid out in a way that's easy to navigate for parents and students browsing on a desktop browser.

Create a web app that shows off what campus life actually looks like, with a photo and video gallery organized by category (like clubs, sports, events, and everyday campus scenes), each item in the gallery has a short caption, and visitors can browse through it all easily from a desktop browser to get a real feel for the school environment.

Need a web app that serves as a campus news reader for a school, where all the latest announcements and stories are listed with titles, dates, and a short summary, the left side has category filters like sports, academics, and events so I can jump to what I care about, and clicking a story opens the full article in the same browser without leaving the app.

Make a web app that lists academic publications from a university or research group, where each entry shows the paper title, authors, year, and a link to read or download it, there's a filter by year or topic area so it's easy to find specific research, and the whole thing works cleanly in a desktop browser for anyone browsing the institution's scholarly output.

A school admissions website where prospective students and parents can see all the enrollment info they need, like application deadlines, requirements, tuition details, and a short step-by-step overview of how to apply, plus a section showing key facts about the school such as class sizes and available programs, all in one place for desktop browser browsing.

Build a web app to promote a specific course or program at an educational institution, where the main area explains what the course covers, who it's for, and what students will walk away knowing, there's a clear list of topics covered week by week, and a spot to sign up or get more info, all designed to work nicely on a desktop browser.

Need a web app that lets students browse and buy courses without the hassle of jumping between pages, the course listing on the left shows categories and prices, clicking a course opens a details area with what's included and a buy button, and after purchasing the course appears right away in a simple list of things I've enrolled in, all in a desktop browser.

Need a web app that works like a small online shop for school supplies and branded merchandise, where items are organized by type (textbooks, stationery, and school gear), each item has a photo, price, and a button to add it to a cart, and checkout is straightforward so students can order what they need from a desktop browser without any confusion.

Need a web app where prospective students or parents can book a slot to visit the school on an open day, it shows a calendar with the available dates and time slots, lets the user fill in their name and contact info, and sends a confirmation right there on screen after booking, all working smoothly in a desktop browser so the process doesn't feel annoying.

Make a web app that lets people book a free trial class or quick consultation with a teacher or advisor, where the main screen shows available time slots on a simple calendar, the user picks a slot and fills in their name and what they want to discuss, and then gets a confirmation shown right on the screen, easy to use in a desktop browser without any friction.

Need a web app that works as an online course platform where I can see all the courses I'm enrolled in from a sidebar, click into any course to watch video lessons in the main area, and track which lessons I've already finished with a simple checkmark so I always know where I left off, and the whole thing runs in a desktop browser without needing any extra software.

A learning management system for a school, browser-based and running on desktop, where students have a home screen listing all their enrolled courses with progress shown for each one, clicking a course opens the lessons in order with readings and assignments listed underneath, and there's a simple way to mark things as done so everyone can stay on top of what's left.

Need a web app where graduates and alumni from a school can find each other and connect, it's a browser-based tool that lets users create a simple profile with their graduation year, major, and what they're up to now, there's a directory where you can search by city or field of work, and a way to send a message or leave a note on someone's profile.

Create a web app that works as a student community hub for a school, where students can post questions, share resources, and chat about campus stuff in topic-based areas like study tips, events, and housing, there's a left-side list of topics to jump between, and each post shows the student's name and the date so it's easy to follow along in a desktop browser.

Make a web app that works as a student portal where everything a student needs is in one place on a desktop browser, like upcoming class schedule, recent grades, announcements from teachers, and links to key resources, with a sidebar to switch between each area quickly so I stop having to log into three separate school systems just to check my timetable.

Make a web app that handles course scheduling for a school, where students can see all available classes listed with times and teachers, pick the ones they want to add to their schedule, and view a weekly timetable that shows everything they've chosen side by side, all running in a desktop browser so nobody has to deal with paper forms or clunky old school systems.

Create a website that serves as an author or editor's personal homepage, with a warm editorial feel like a well-designed literary magazine, showing a short bio, a curated list of published articles or books grouped by topic, and a way to get in touch, laid out in a clean and slightly understated style that lets the writing take center stage when viewed in a desktop browser.

Need a web app that displays an awards and recognition archive for a media outlet or publication, with a tasteful gallery-style layout where each award entry has the year, the prize name, and what it was given for, grouped by category and presented with enough visual breathing room that it feels prestigious rather than cluttered, all for viewing comfortably in a desktop browser.

Make a web app that works as a news portal with an editorial feel that actually makes reading feel worthwhile, where the home screen has a featured story at the top with a strong image and headline, a row of secondary stories below it organized by topic, and a left sidebar with category links so readers can jump to what interests them, all designed for a desktop browser experience with good visual rhythm.

Make a web app that feels like a real online magazine, with a rich visual layout for desktop browsers where the cover story gets a big full-width image and bold headline, the rest of the issue is organized into sections with editorial photos and pull quotes, and readers can flip through pieces in a way that feels curated and intentional rather than just a plain list of links.

Create a web app that acts as a subscription wall for a media or content site, with a design that feels editorial and classy rather than aggressive, showing a teaser of the article or content behind it, a short explanation of what subscribers get access to, and a clean sign-up area with a couple of tier options, all presented in a way that makes becoming a subscriber feel like a natural next step on a desktop browser.

Build a web app that works as a membership page for a media brand, with a look that feels warm and inviting like a quality publication you actually want to support, showing the different membership tiers with what each one includes, a few quotes from existing members, and a straightforward way to join, all designed for desktop browsers with a visual style that feels considered and not generic.

Make a paid subscription manager web app for desktop browsers where I can see all my active subscriptions in one place, track when each one renews, and quickly cancel or pause the ones I forget about until I get the charge on my credit card, with a simple list showing the service name, cost, and next billing date.

Build a book and culture merchandise shop web app where I can browse titles and creative goods, add things to a cart, and check out without having to jump between five different sites, with a clean product listing that shows price and a short description so I can decide fast.

Make an interview booking tool as a web app where journalists and PR contacts can see my available time slots, pick one that works, and fill in their name and the topic they want to cover, so I stop going back and forth on email just to lock down a 30-minute call.

Make a press conference seat reservation app for desktop browsers where credentialed journalists can log in with their press ID, browse upcoming events, and claim a seat without having to call anyone, with each event showing the date, location, and how many seats are still open.

Make a knowledge topic hub web app where I can browse articles and resources organized by subject area, see a table of contents on the side so I know what topics are covered, and save the ones I want to read later to a personal list, all in one tidy browser-based tool I can keep open on my desktop.

Build a long-form journalism collection app for desktop browsers where I can store and browse in-depth investigative articles, organize them by theme or publication, and mark the ones I have read so I can keep track of what I still want to get through, with each entry showing the title, author, and a short summary.

Build a reader comment section app as a web app where people can leave comments on articles, reply to each other in threads, and vote comments up so the best ones float to the top, the kind of thing I want to add to a small publication site running in a desktop browser.

Create a user-submitted content tool as a web app where anyone can write and submit a short article or story, include a title and a few tags to describe what it is about, and see their submission show up in a browsable feed once it goes live, all accessible from a desktop browser.

Make an RSS feed aggregator app that runs in a browser so I can paste in a bunch of feed URLs from the news sites and blogs I follow, have all the latest posts show up in one scrollable list sorted by time, and never have to open ten separate tabs just to catch up on things in the morning.

Make a news search tool as a web app for desktop browsers where I can type in a keyword and get back a list of matching articles from multiple sources, each showing the headline, the outlet, and how recent it is, so I can quickly find what happened on a specific topic without hunting through individual sites.

Create a museum website app with a calm, editorial look, something that feels like a well-designed printed catalogue rather than a generic corporate site, where visitors browsing on a desktop can explore current and upcoming exhibitions, see beautiful full-width images for each show, and find practical details like hours and location in a clean sidebar.

Create an art festival website app that feels bold and immersive, with rich visuals and a strong visual identity that sets the mood before anyone reads a single word, where desktop visitors can browse the lineup of events, click into each one for details, and get a sense of the whole festival as one cohesive experience.

Historical archive browser app for desktop, the kind of thing that feels like opening a well-preserved collection rather than a generic file list, where you can explore documents and photos organized along a timeline and browse by era or topic, with each entry displaying a thumbnail and a short contextual note so the material feels alive rather than just catalogued.

Create a research publication web app for desktop browsers that feels considered and quiet, like a serious academic journal but with a layout that is actually pleasant to read, where each published piece has a clean reading view with the author, date, and an abstract up top, and visitors can browse all work sorted by topic or date.

Build a fundraising campaign web app for desktop browsers that carries real warmth and purpose, the kind of site that makes a donor feel their contribution matters and not just like a transaction, with a clear story section at the top, a live progress bar showing how close the campaign is to its goal, and a simple giving form below.

An advocacy campaign tracker for desktop browsers, the kind of app that feels like it belongs to a cause and not a corporation, where supporters can read the core message, sign onto the campaign, and see a running count of people who have already joined, with the whole thing having a focused identity that makes the cause feel real and worth joining.

Make a museum gift shop web app for desktop browsers where visitors can browse souvenirs and print reproductions by category, see a clear photo and price for each item, and add things to a cart so they can buy something even after they have left the building and no longer have to remember the shop's website separately.

Need a ticket sales app for a web browser where people can see a list of upcoming events with dates, prices, and available seats, pick the ones they want, enter their details, and get a confirmation, so the whole purchase takes under two minutes and nobody has to call a box office.

Make a museum visit booking web app where people can pick a date, choose a time slot, say how many tickets they need, and get a confirmation right away, all from a desktop browser, so I stop dealing with phone calls and manual reservation sheets for a venue that gets a steady stream of group visits.

Create an event sign-up web app for desktop browsers where people can see a list of upcoming cultural events, click on one they want to join, fill in their name and contact info, and get a confirmation, so organizers always know exactly who is coming and attendees have a record of what they registered for.

Need a science education resource app for desktop browsers where I can find articles, videos, and guides organized by topic, see a clear list of what is available under each subject, and save the ones I want to use with students so I have a reliable place to pull lesson materials without digging through random search results every time.

Create a digital archive web app for desktop browsers where I can upload and organize historical documents and photos, browse them by year or category, and search by keyword to find a specific item fast, with each entry showing a title, date, and short description so the collection stays easy to navigate as it grows.

Make a volunteer community web app where people interested in cultural events can browse open volunteer opportunities, sign up for the ones they want to help with, and see a feed of updates from the group, the kind of browser-based tool that makes it easy for a small organization to coordinate help from regulars and new faces alike.

Build a topic discussion forum app for desktop browsers where people can post about cultural and civic issues, reply to each other in threads, and browse discussions sorted by subject area, the kind of web app a small community group could use to keep ongoing conversations in one place rather than scattered across group chats.

Make a public services portal web app for desktop browsers where residents can find information about local government services in one place, search by topic to get to the right form or contact quickly, and see a list of the most-used services on the home screen so nobody has to click through five levels of menus just to figure out how to renew a permit.
